title: Can Astra Solve RoboMME without Breaking the Bank?
review_scope: Primary manuscript introduction, methods in Sections 2.3–2.4 and evaluation limitations in Section 4 reviewed. No independent reproduction or accepted-version confirmation.
summary: Astra/RoboMME separates subtask reasoning, progress monitoring and action execution. A LoRA-fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct monitor, called System 1.5 by the authors, checks each action chunk while π0.5 retains the current subtask instruction. Completion or task-specific events can trigger another Astra decision. The monitor is a particular implementation with learned supervision and task configuration, rather than a standard layer required by every robot. The simulator pauses while Astra reasons, and the paper does not provide matched monitor-versus-always-replan ablations, monetary or token-cost measurements, or a full account of monitor errors in a continuously running loop.
method: Use an adapted vision-language monitor to check action chunks and trigger higher-level subtask reasoning on completion or configured events.
why_it_matters: Makes the monitoring interface between slower reasoning and an action policy explicit.
open_question: How well do the monitor and replanning rules work when physical dynamics continue during reasoning?
limitations: Task-specific history, prompt templates and event rules remain part of the setup.
The simulator pauses during higher-level planning.
Matched ablations, monetary/token-cost measurements and monitor-error evaluation remain incomplete.

title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
review_scope: Primary manuscript introduction, execution methods in Sections 4A–4B and reported evaluation/limitations reviewed. No independent reproduction or accepted-version confirmation.
summary: AMP1 keeps an agent in the manipulation loop through a persistent Python interpreter. Generated programs call sensing, perception and motion APIs and produce timed end-effector and gripper waypoints. An engineered backend supplies inverse kinematics, trajectory checks and controller execution. This is code-mediated control through an existing robot interface; writing the program does not replace those physical-control components. AMP1+ retains notes and code between episodes while the language-model weights stay fixed. Reasoning latency and the capabilities of the supplied harness remain important constraints on deployment.
method: Generate and execute Python programs against perception and motion APIs, with waypoint execution handled by the robot backend.
why_it_matters: Provides a concrete example of an agent writing executable behavior while reusing existing robot interfaces.
open_question: How does code-mediated execution behave when reasoning delays and backend constraints dominate the physical task?
limitations: Reasoning latency remains a deployment constraint.
The backend retains inverse kinematics, trajectory checks and motion controllers.
AMP1+ changes retained notes and code, while the language-model weights stay fixed.

title: Scaling Online Exploration for Robot Agents
review_scope: Primary manuscript introduction, exploration/compilation methods in Sections 3.3–3.4 and evaluation setup in Section 4 reviewed. No independent reproduction or accepted-version confirmation.
summary: RAX explores and debugs programs, compiles successful decisions into modular executable skills, and retains notes and a verified skill repository. Its language-model parameters remain fixed: the reusable artifact is programmatic experience, rather than a newly trained neural policy checkpoint. The robot backend supplies control and safeguards, and real motion requires operator arming. Task inputs can include goal images or visual demonstrations; the HumanoidArena evaluation uses three teleoperated demonstrations per task. Repository admission checks successful unattended execution and supporting evidence or preconditions, but this does not establish reliability in arbitrary new environments.
method: Explore and debug programs, verify successful executions, and compile reusable modular skills while retaining structured experience.
why_it_matters: Separates program and skill discovery from numerical policy training.
open_question: Which retained programs remain useful when the environment or the original skill preconditions change?
limitations: Language-model parameters stay fixed; notes and programs are the retained artifacts.
Real motion requires operator arming and an engineered control backend.
HumanoidArena uses three teleoperated demonstrations per task.
Verified repository admission does not guarantee transfer to arbitrary new environments.
